land.text: the Pandya country round Madurai: 'the Cholas had lost most of their control of the territories south of the river Kaveri' as Pandya power rose (Rajaraja III page)

predecessors.note: Maravarman Sundara Pandyan I 'succeeded his older brother Jatavarman Kulasekhara in 1216'. The chola-empire dossier (sa-03) records the loss in 1216. The earlier Pandya state is pandya-dynasty (592-915); the 'Pandya Empire' and 'Pandya Dynasty' rows share Wikidata Q844910 but are separated by three centuries of Chola rule, so they are different states of one dynasty.

land.text: the Pandya country, which Ulugh Khan 'annexed ... as the Ma'bar province'

successors.note: Madurai Sultanate page: proclaimed 1335 by Jalaluddin Ahsan Khan after the Tughlaq province; the Pandyas 'moved their capital to Tenkasi and kept a small territory until the end of the 16th century' (Pandya Empire page, not drawn here).

capitals.name: Madurai
capitals.note: 'Madurai was the main capital. Kanchi was a secondary capital in the 13th century' ('Kanchi became the second major city of the kingdom' under Jatavarman Sundara I); Korkai was a port; Tenkasi was the last capital after the Tughlaq conquest. Coordinates approximate.

rulers.name: Maravarman Sundara Pandyan I
rulers.note: 'succeeded his older brother Jatavarman Kulasekhara in 1216'; the end year is not given (Sundara Pandyan II 'acceded to power in 1238').

rulers.name: Maravarman Sundara Pandyan II
rulers.note: Crowned July/August 1238; reign 1238-1251 on the infobox, 'His years of reign are unclear'; shared with Jatavarman Kulasekaran II 1238-1240 and Sadayavarman Vikkiraman I 1241-1250.

rulers.name: Jatavarman Sundara Pandyan I
rulers.note: 'acceded to the Pandyan throne in the year 1251 CE', coronation 20-28 April 1251; succeeded by Kulasekara in 1268 and 'died in 1271' on the same page.

rulers.name: Sundara Pandya IV and Vira Pandya IV
rulers.note: Sons who fought for the throne after 1310; Sundara Pandya prevailed 'after a short period'; reign years not given.

keyframe_review.note: 218k km2 for 1314-1325; Kerala is lost ('The Pandyas lost south Kerala in 1312'). 'Sundara Pandya sought Khalji help and regained the South Arcot region by 1314' (no loss is dated, so none is drawn). The shape ends in 1325: the page dates the sultanate expeditions of 1314 and 1323 and the annexation as the Ma'bar province without a year; Ulugh Khan became sultan in 1325 (Madurai Sultanate page). Hoysala land removed (repair fx-28): the Pandya page says the Pandyas were 'successful in confining the Hoysala control to the Mysore Plateau' and the Hoysala page never has them holding the Mysore plateau, so the 172 cells of Cliopatria's outline that lie inside the Hoysala heartland (Karnataka 151, Kerala 10, Tamil Nadu 11) are cut out. Kannanur removed for this start year (repair fx-28): the Pandya ledger loses it again c. 1295 ('Toward the end of the 13th century, Veera Ballala III recaptured territory in the Tamil country which had been lost during a Pandya uprising', Hoysala page; ledger 18), so the Hoysalas hold it again in 1312-1313.

ledger.note: 1216: Maravarman Sundara Pandyan I succeeds and the Pandyas rise over the Cholas. 'He succeeded his older brother Jatavarman Kulasekhara in 1216'; the page does not name a 'Second Pandyan Empire' or give 1216-1345 (infobox: 400 BCE-1618 CE), and it describes this period as the 'Later Pandyas'.

region.text: Uraiyur and Thanjavur in the Kaveri delta

ledger.note: 1216 (year bridged): the Pandyas invade the Chola country. 'He invaded the Chola country, sacked Uraiyur and Thanjavur, and drove Chola king Kulothunga III into exile' (undated); the Rajaraja III page: 'Pandya army entered the Chola capital and Rajaraja took flight' (July 1216 accession). The chola-empire dossier dates the sack 1215-1216.

region.text: the Chola kingdom left after the Pandya sack

ledger.note: 1216 (year bridged): the Chola king submits. 'Kulothunga later submitted and accepted Pandya overlordship' (undated on the page). [Repair sa-04-a, thin finding: the Maravarman Sundara Pandyan page has 'Kulothunga made his formal submission to Pandyan rule in 1217 CE at Pon Amaravathi' and his death in 1218; the year stays 1216 so that it matches chola-empire ledger 36 until the two are settled together (the submission may be 1217).]

region.text: the Chola country on the Kaveri

ledger.note: 1217 (year bridged): Mahendramangalam. Rajaraja III, 'backed by Hoysala king Narasimha II, fought the Pandyas at Mahendramangalam on the Kaveri. The Pandyas lost, and Rajaraja III was restored.' The page gives no year; 1217 is the year of Veera Ballala II's victory in the hoysala-kingdom dossier. [Repair sa-04-a, thin finding: the same page dates the battle of Mahendramangalam, where 'Narasimha himself defeated Sundara Pandiyan ... in 1231 CE' (Hoysala Vira Narasimha II, who ruled 1220-1235), after Rajaraja III's capture at Tellaru in 1231; the 1217 here is Veera Ballala II's victory in the Hoysala Empire page (via chola-empire ledger 37), so the Mahendramangalam of this note is probably the 1231 battle and the restoration of Rajaraja III may be 1231. Unsettled; chola-empire (sa-03) and this ledger bridge 1217.]

1217 (year bridged): the Chola overlordship ends with the restoration of Rajaraja III at Mahendramangalam. [Repair sa-04-a, thin finding: see the contest_end of 1217: the Maravarman Sundara Pandyan page puts Mahendramangalam and the Hoysala intervention in 1231, so the Chola overlordship may run to 1231.]

ledger.counterpart: unnamed rulers of the Pandya south and the Kerala coast
ledger.note: 1220 (Cliopatria year): Tirunelveli and the Kerala coast join the Madurai country. No page dates it; the Sundara II page has Hoysala hegemony over the Pandya country 'from about 1220 to 1245'.

About 1220: the Pandyas pay tribute to the Hoysala king. Sastri (Sundara II page): Hoysala influence 'increased steadily from about 1220 to 1245', and 'Pandyan inscriptions of the period' indicate 'tribute being paid to' the Hoysala king (Vira Someshwara). The page gives the span, not a treaty; the region is the Pandya country of the years (Cliopatria's shape). Mirror of hoysala-kingdom ledger 1220. [Repair sa-04-a, reviewer finding: the Hoysala hegemony over the Pandyas was missing from the ledger although KF1 quotes it.]
1236 (Cliopatria year): Kongu and Palakkad. The Jatavarman page has 'Bana (Magadai) and Kongu came under Pandya rule' during the wars of Sundara I (1251-1268), without a year.

region.text: the Kaveri delta round Thanjavur, Salem, Erode and the far south

ledger.note: 1241 (Cliopatria year): the Kaveri delta and the north of the Kongu plateau. Maravarman Sundara I 'sacked Uraiyur and Thanjavur' (undated); the chola-empire dossier records the loss c. 1241 (bridged).

About 1245: the Hoysala hegemony over the Pandyas ends. The same sentence gives the span 'from about 1220 to 1245'; Sundara II 'acceded to power in 1238' and was 'attacked and defeated' by Rajendra Chola III around 1250. Mirror of hoysala-kingdom ledger 1245.

region.text: Kanchipuram and the Chola north: Chidambaram, Cuddalore, Arcot, Tiruvannamalai, Chennai

ledger.note: 1258: Kanchipuram. 'Pandyan forces killed the Telugu Choda ruler Vijaya Gandagopala of Nellore Chodas and captured Kanchipuram in 1258.' Kanchi became the second city of the kingdom. The wider northern zone is Cliopatria's 1250 shape, which the chola-empire dossier records as 'by 1250'. [Reviewer sa-04-a: confidence 3 to 2: the page names Kanchipuram (and 'Kanchi, Nellore and Visayavadai' without a year), not Chidambaram, Cuddalore or Arcot, which the region (Cliopatria's 1250 delta) takes in]

1258: Nellore. The Nellore Choda ruler was killed in 1258 and Nellore was annexed ('Kanchi, Nellore, and Visayavadai were annexed'); 'a Kakatiya army' was beaten 'at Mudugur in the Nellore district' (undated). The kakatiya-dynasty dossier dates the Pandya capture of Nellore 1263 (Muttukuru).

region.text: the Chola remnant north of Kanchi

ledger.note: c. 1258-1260: the last Cholas pay tribute. 'He subdued Chola Rajendra II c. 1258-1260 and made him pay tribute' (the page's 'Rajendra II' is Rajendra III); the Jatavarman page: Rajendra III accepted 'Pandyan overlordship' (no year).

1258: Jaffna becomes a Pandya feudatory. The Jaffna page's lead: 'a tribute-paying feudatory of the Pandyan Empire in 1258' (its body installs Aryacakravarti in 1262, the infobox in 1277); the Parakramabahu II page has Chandrabhanu submit Jaffna 'to Pandya rule as a vassal' after the invasion of 1254-1256.

By 1262: Kannanur. The Pandyas 'seized the Hoysala southern capital, Kannanur Koppam, near Srirangam' (no year); Someshwara's counteroffensive 'in 1262' failed and 'ended in his death'; the Pandya Empire page says he 'was killed by the Pandyas in 1262'.

By 1271 (bridge): Nellore leaves Pandya hands. 'Mahamandaleshvara Naga-deva Maharaja, a vassal of Rudrama, ruled at Nellore during 1271-1275', and 'Kakatiyas regained control over some of the territory that they had earlier lost to the Pandyas' (Rudrama Devi page, no year for the regaining); the kakatiya-dynasty dossier has the Pandyas take Nellore in 1263 and Naga-deva vassal from 1271. The Telugu Chodas and Ambadeva's nominee hold Nellore after 1275 and the Kakatiyas retake it from them in 1290 (kakatiya-dynasty), not from the Pandyas. [Repair sa-04-a, reviewer finding: KF7 removed Nellore with no ledger loss, and its note named the 1290 Kakatiya regain from the Telugu Chodas as the 'mirror'.]
c. 1279: the Cholas end. 'A combined force of Hoysala Ramanatha and Chola Rajendra III was defeated by him c. 1279' (Kulasekara); the chola-empire dossier ends the dynasty then.

1284: the Pandyas take the Tooth Relic. 'Pandyas of South India invaded, captured the Tooth Relic, and carried it to India' (1284); the Pandya Empire page: Kulasekara 'invaded Sri Lanka and carried away the Tooth Relic. Pandya control of Sri Lanka lasted until c. 1308-1309'. The region is my reading: the royal core where the relic was. [Repair sa-04-a, reviewer finding: the counterpart 'ceylon' is now the merged Sinhalese state (kingdom-of-dambadeniya was merged into ceylon, which starts in 1220); the pair 1284-1309 is the one occupation, so no split at 1293/1294 is needed.]

region.text: Kannanur and the Tamil holdings of the Hoysalas

ledger.note: c. 1295 (year bridged): Veera Ballala III recovers the Tamil holdings. 'Pandyan rule over the Hoysala-held region lasted until Veera Ballala III recaptured it near the end of the 13th century'; the hoysala-kingdom dossier places it c. 1295.

c. 1309: Pandya control of Sri Lanka ends. 'Pandya control of Sri Lanka lasted until c. 1308-1309.' [Repair sa-04-a, reviewer finding: the counterpart 'ceylon' is now the merged Sinhalese state (kingdom-of-dambadeniya was merged into ceylon, which starts in 1220); the pair 1284-1309 is the one occupation, so no split at 1293/1294 is needed.]
March 1311: Malik Kafur's army enters the Pandya country. 'Khalji forces marched into Pandya territory in March 1311. The Pandya brothers fled, and the pursuit failed.'
Late April 1311: the Khaljis return to Delhi with plunder. 'By late April 1311 the Khaljis returned to Delhi with plunder.'

region.text: south Kerala inside the Pandya outline

ledger.counterpart: rulers of south Kerala (not named by the page)
ledger.note: 1312: south Kerala is lost. 'The Pandyas lost south Kerala in 1312.' The page does not name the new holders.

c. 1317: the Kakatiyas occupy Kanchi. 'After Alauddin's death in 1316, the Hoysala king Ballala launched a fresh invasion of the Pandya territory'; the Kakatiya commander Peda Rudra defeated Ballala, 'After this victory, he occupied Kanchi in the Pandya territory'; Devarinayaka 'defeated Vira Pandya' and the Kakatiyas 'reinstated Sundara Pandya at Viradhavala'; the grant of 1317 is the only dated item (the page dates the occupation itself to no year). Mirror of kakatiya-dynasty ledger c. 1317. [Repair sa-04-a, reviewer finding: Kakatiya occupation of Kanchi had no mirror.]
1323: the Jaffna kingdom is independent. 'In 1323 the Jaffna kingdom declared independence, and north Sri Lanka was lost' (the Jaffna infobox: independence from the Pandya dynasty 1323).
1323: the Tughlaq army comes south. 'Further sultanate expeditions came in 1314 (Khusro Khan) and 1323 (Jauna Khan, under Ghiyath al-Din Tughluq).'

1323 (bridge): the Kanchi occupation ends with the Kakatiya kingdom. 'When the Pandya forces tried to evict the Kakatiyas from Kanchi, Prataparudra himself led an army against them'; the page gives no end date. Mirror of kakatiya-dynasty ledger 1323.

By 1325: the conquest is complete. The Pandya page: Ulugh Khan, 'later Muhammad bin Tughluq, annexed the former Pandya lands as the Ma'bar province' (no year); the Madurai Sultanate page has Jauna Khan become sultan in 1325, which bounds it. Confidence 1.

region.text: the Pandya country annexed as Ma'bar

ledger.note: By 1325: the Pandya Empire becomes the Ma'bar province. The annexation is undated on the pages opened (bounded by the 1323 expedition and Ulugh Khan's accession in 1325); the Madurai Sultanate follows in 1335 ('proclaimed in 1335 in Madurai, led by Jalaluddin Ahsan Khan') and the Pandyas keep a small territory at Tenkasi. [Repair sa-04-a, thin finding: the Muhammad bin Tughluq page was opened: 'ascended the throne ... on 4 February 1325' and 'In 1334, there was a rebellion in Mabar'; it has no date for the annexation of Ma'bar, so 1325 stays a bound.]

wars.name: Pandya-Chola-Hoysala war of 1216-1217
wars.outcome: The Pandyas sack Uraiyur and Thanjavur; Kulothunga III accepts Pandya overlordship; Rajaraja III, backed by the Hoysala Narasimha II, defeats them at Mahendramangalam on the Kaveri and is restored.
wars.note: No year on the pages opened; 1216-1217 follows the chola-empire and hoysala-kingdom dossiers.

wars.name: Pandyan conquest of the Chola north and Nellore

zones.text: Kanchipuram and the Chola north: Chidambaram, Cuddalore, Arcot, Tiruvannamalai, Chennai

wars.outcome: Kanchipuram taken and the Nellore Choda ruler killed in 1258; Rajendra III pays tribute c. 1258-1260; the Kakatiya army beaten at Mudugur; the Pandya extent 'till Nellore and Kadapa'.

wars.name: Pandya-Hoysala war over Kannanur
wars.outcome: The Pandyas take Kannanur; Someshwara's counteroffensive of 1262 fails and he is killed; Ramanatha recovers Kannanur later.
wars.note: Start year is mine (the seizure of Kannanur is undated).

wars.name: Pandya invasions of Sri Lanka
wars.outcome: Intervention of 1258, Veera Pandyan's of 1262-1264 and again 1270 (Jatavarman page); Tooth Relic taken in 1284; Pandya control to c. 1308-1309.

wars.name: Pandya succession war and the Khalji invasion
wars.outcome: Sundara Pandya IV defeats his brother Vira Pandya IV; Malik Kafur raids the country in March-April 1311; Sundara regains South Arcot with Khalji help by 1314; Ballala III, who invaded the Pandya country, retreats to his capital.

wars.name: Tughlaq conquest of the Pandya country
wars.outcome: Expeditions of 1314 (Khusro Khan) and 1323 (Jauna Khan); the Pandya lands become the Ma'bar province before 1325.

certainty.note: No Pandya frontier is on the pages; the shapes are Cliopatria's. The Chola, Hoysala and Telugu marches change hands without lines.

notes:
Cliopatria's 'Pandya Empire' (1216-1325) is the Second Pandyan Empire; its Wikidata id Q844910 is shared with 'Pandya Dynasty' (pandya-dynasty, 592-915). They are different states of one dynasty: no Cliopatria shape lies between 921 and 1216, the Cholas ruled the Pandya country in between, and the pandya-dynasty dossier already lists only 'Pandya Dynasty' in its cliopatria_names; this dossier therefore lists only 'Pandya Empire', and the colour agent should give it the same family and hue (rule 2). The Pandya Empire page (a redirect to the Pandya dynasty article) has no 'Second Pandyan Empire' label and no dates for 1216-1345. Pages opened: 7 (the five for this state, plus the Dambadeniya and Jaffna pages opened for the Sri Lankan dossiers). WEAK SPOTS: (1) The growth from 1216 to 1250 (Tirunelveli, Kongu, the Kaveri delta) is not dated by any page opened; the events are confidence 1 and carry the Cliopatria year; the sack of Thanjavur and the Mahendramangalam battle are undated on the pages (1216/1217 come from the chola-empire and hoysala-kingdom dossiers); (2) the 1250 shape is held back to 1258 on the strength of the Jatavarman page ('captured Kanchipuram in 1258'), while the chola-empire dossier says 'by 1250'; (3) Nellore: the Jatavarman page annexes it in 1258, the kakatiya-dynasty dossier has the Pandyas take it in 1263 at Muttukuru and lose it in 1290; no page opened dates the loss; (4) Sri Lanka: the Pandya Empire page says control lasted to c. 1308-1309 but gives no region; the occupation is drawn on the Dambadeniya country only, with the Jaffna peninsula as a vassal from 1258 (Jaffna page lead) to 1323; (5) the Hoysala hegemony over the Pandya country 1220-1245 (Sundara II page, Sastri) is recorded in the hoysala-kingdom dossier, not here; (6) the end: no page dates the annexation as the Ma'bar province, so 1325 (Cliopatria's last year, one year after the 1323 expedition and the year Ulugh Khan becomes sultan) is confidence 1; the Madurai Sultanate (1335) and the Tenkasi Pandyas (to 1618) are not drawn; (7) the Kakatiya occupation of Kanchi c. 1317-1323 (kakatiya-dynasty dossier) is not on a page opened here. South Arcot (lost and regained by 1314) is in the shape throughout. Mirrors: chola-empire carries the 1216/1217 and c. 1258-1279 events; hoysala-kingdom the 1262 and c. 1295 transfers; ceylon and kingdom-of-dambadeniya the 1284-c. 1309 occupation; jaffna-kingdom (sa-04, another part) should carry the 1258-1323 vassalage and the 1323 independence. Gazetteer: no new names.

Repair pass (sa-04-a, 2026-10-19): Hoysala tribute 1220-1245 added (vassal_start/vassal_end, source the Sundara II page); Nellore loss added (1271, confidence 1, to kakatiya-dynasty on the Rudrama Devi page) and KF7 split at 1271 (renamed pandya-empire_1271); Kakatiya occupation of Kanchi 1317-1323 added (Prataparudra II page); the Sri Lanka occupation names the merged ceylon dossier. Not settled: the Nellore capture is 1258 on the Jatavarman page (Telugu Chodas) and 1263 on the kakatiya dossier (Ganapati Deva page); the Rudrama Devi page gives no year for either.

Thin findings tried (sa-04-a repair): the Maravarman Sundara Pandyan page dates Kulothunga's submission to 1217 and Mahendramangalam to 1231 (Narasimha II), against the 1216/1217 bridge used here and in chola-empire; Tirunelveli, Kongu and the Kaveri delta are on no page (the events stay confidence 1); the Muhammad bin Tughluq page has no annexation date; South Arcot by 1314 was not re-read.
